verdict.rationale: Babylon.js documents browser rendering on WebGL 1.0, WebGL 2.0 and WebGPU, and offers tree-shakable ES6 modules to help control bundle size. Payload is a real caveat: a hands-on user reports it is about three times the size of Three.js and needs bandwidth optimization, and the vendor itself acknowledged scene-format size and load-time issues. Missing for 10: in-depth WebGPU documentation or independent corroboration of WebGPU maturity, concrete bundle-size figures or evidence that tree-shaking yields a reasonable payload.

support.subject: As a web developer, my game runs in the browser with a reasonable payload — WebGL today, and a credible WebGPU story
